business.description: Pioneer Embroideries Limited is one of India's leading manufacturers and exporters of value-added Specialised Polyester Filament Yarn (SPFY) and Embroidery & Laces (EL), operating across two complementary business verticals with nationally recognised brands SILKOLITE (yarn) and HAKOBA (embroidery retail).

products.note: Includes standard range (DTY, FDY, POY, Twisted Yarns) and specialty/value-added (Air Texturised, Carpet, Dope-Dyed, Thermal, Camouflage, Flame Retardant, Anti-Microbial/UV-Stabilised, Biodegradable, Recycled) and sustainable products

products.note: Includes Schiffli Embroidery, Fabric Allover & Laces, Guipure Allover & Laces, Braided Laces (Bobbin Laces), Fancy Laces, and Hakoba retail products (sarees, SKDs, fashion fabrics, men's ethnic wear)

outlook.statement: US-India trade negotiations progressing with partial reversal of some tariff categories in late 2025 and early 2026 generating renewed export enquiries; India's textile sector at inflection point with China Plus One diversification creating generational opportunity; PM MITRA Parks, PLI Scheme, National Technical Textiles Mission, Cotton Mission, and India-UK FTA (signed July 2025 granting duty-free access to 99% of India's textile exports) reinforcing long-term growth foundations; global textile trade expected to reach US$1.2 trillion by 2030; India targets tripling textile exports from ₹3 lakh crore to ₹9 lakh crore by 2030

Priorities for FY27: drive domestic growth in SPFY, improve export performance, increase utilisation at Degaon facility, strengthen Hakoba brand, realise benefits of green energy investments, continue focus on cost optimisation, working capital discipline and debt reduction

Primary objective is to recover and grow export revenues as US-India trade negotiations progress and tariff headwinds ease; deepen domestic volumes across key textile clusters with emphasis on increasing share of value-added specialty products in revenue mix
Central priority is building utilisation of Degaon facility toward designed operating level; actively developing new customer relationships for eight-machine embroidery configuration
Focus on investing in Hakoba brand's digital and distribution presence to return franchise to growth, leveraging 300,000+ design library and heritage positioning

Deleveraging trajectory will be maintained and accelerated where cash generation permits; target continued meaningful reduction in total debt through FY27 with operating free cash flow augmented by full-year benefit of green energy savings

India's domestic textile & apparel market estimated at US$157 billion in FY25-26, growing at ~7% CAGR. India's textile & apparel market projected to grow at 11.98% CAGR, reaching $646.96 billion by 2033. Global textile & apparel market valued at US$1.9 trillion in 2025, expected to grow at 4.1% CAGR from 2026-2034. Global textile & apparel trade expected to grow at 4% CAGR to reach US$1.2 trillion by 2030. India targets exports of US$105 billion by 2030.

Company focused on operational excellence, cost optimisation, value-added product expansion and manufacturing efficiency. Modernised Degaon facility and commissioning of green energy infrastructure in May 2026 position the Company to improve operating leverage, strengthen competitiveness and drive sustainable long-term growth.

Credit risk: The Company reviews customer creditworthiness before offering standard payment terms; sale limits are established per customer and reviewed periodically; any sales exceeding limits require approval from the President. More than 60% of customers have been transacting for over four years with no impairment loss recognized.

Liquidity risk: The Company manages liquidity by maintaining sufficient cash, marketable securities, and committed credit facilities; monitors rolling forecasts of liquidity position and cash equivalents; projects cash flows in major currencies and monitors balance sheet liquidity ratios.

Market risk: The Company is exposed to foreign exchange risk primarily with respect to USD and small exposure in EUR and GBP; uses forward contracts to manage foreign exchange risk; currency risks related to foreign currency payables have been partially hedged using forward contracts.

Interest rate risk: The Company's main interest rate risk arises from long-term borrowings with variable rates denominated in Indian Rupees; currently borrowings are within acceptable risk levels and no swaps have been taken to hedge interest rate risk.
